1.why: MFA routes use requireSession(request, true) and bind solely to session.userId with no client-supplied account id.

2.why: Identity codes are per-session, TOTP is tied to the account secret, and recovery codes are per-account hashes, so codes do not work across users.

3.why: enrol/verify sets mfaEnabled and secrets on the account but never deletes or invalidates other existing sessions.

4.why: OTP secrets are stored via AES-GCM encryptAtRest and recovery codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes.

5.why: Tokens, OTP secrets, recovery codes, and six-digit codes are produced with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no secrets/OTPs/session tokens are written to localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, recovery code, and password with strict validators before use.

8.why: Client assigns untrusted values with textContent and the shell HTML is static/nonce-based, so markup is not interpreted as HTML.

9.why: No redirect responses or open redirect parameters exist; navigation stays on same-origin API/page routes.

10.why: baseHeaders sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY and frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: sessionCookie sets HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict on bank_session.

12.why: Server errors are generic and avoid stack traces, but the UI testLog/API mocks deliberately surface identity codes, OTP secrets, and recovery codes in page logs.

13.why: Identity codes have expiresAt and consumed; TOTP periods are time-bound and recorded in usedOtpPeriods; recovery codes are removed on redeem.

14.why: Sign-in, identity, OTP, and recovery paths increment failure counters and apply LOCKOUT_MS after MAX_FAILURES.

15.why: Sign-in mints a new session id, idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in requireSession, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
